claim: OpenSearch is an open source, distributed search and analytics suite derived from Elasticsearch.

evidence.quote: OpenSearch is an open source, distributed search and analytics suite derived from Elasticsearch.

claim: OpenSearch Service lets you deploy instances across one, two, or three AZs: development or test workloads can use the single AZ option, and production-grade workloads should use two or three AZs.
question: Which Availability Zone deployment options does Amazon OpenSearch Service offer and which suit production?

values.display: production-grade workloads should use two or three AZs

evidence.quote: Amazon OpenSearch Service offers customers the option to deploy their instances across one, two, or three AZs. Customers running development or test workloads can pick the single AZ option. Those running production-grade workloads should use two or three AZs.

claim: Three AZ deployments are strongly recommended for workloads with higher availability requirements.

values.display: Three AZ deployments are strongly recommended

evidence.quote: Three AZ deployments are strongly recommended for workloads with higher availability requirements.

claim: The three AZ option is only available in Regions where there are three or more AZs.

values.display: only available in regions where there are three or more AZs

evidence.quote: Note: The three AZ option is only available in regions where there are three or more AZs.

claim: OpenSearch Service is integrated with Amazon VPC: with VPC access, IP addresses from your VPC are attached to the domain and all network traffic stays within the AWS network and is not accessible to the Internet.
question: Does Amazon OpenSearch Service support Amazon VPC and what happens to the traffic?

values.display: IP addresses from your VPC are attached

evidence.quote: Yes, Amazon OpenSearch Service is integrated with Amazon VPC. When choosing VPC access, IP addresses from your VPC are attached to your Amazon OpenSearch Service domain and all network traffic stays within the AWS network and is not accessible to the Internet.

claim: You can configure dedicated master nodes for your domains, and when you choose a dedicated master configuration you specify the instance type and instance count.
question: Does Amazon OpenSearch Service support configuring dedicated master nodes?

evidence.quote: You can configure dedicated master nodes for your domains. When choosing a dedicated master configuration, you can specify the instance type and instance count.

note: The FAQ answer uses the former name Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose; the current name is Amazon Data Firehose.

evidence.quote: You can use native Elasticsearch (up to version 7.10) or OpenSearch APIs, such as the index and bulk APIs, to load data into your domain.

increase and decrease the size of the storage volume

claim: For production workloads, AWS recommends deploying data instances across three AZs for better availability, and provisioning instances in multiples of three for equal distribution across AZs.
question: What is the recommended AZ configuration for production OpenSearch Service workloads?

regions where three AZs are not available

claim: If one or more instances in an AZ are unreachable or not functional, OpenSearch Service automatically tries to bring up new instances in the same AZ to replace the affected instances.
question: How does Amazon OpenSearch Service handle instance failures?

values.display: bring up new instances in the same AZ

evidence.quote: If one or more instances in an AZ are unreachable or not functional, Amazon OpenSearch Service automatically tries to bring up new instances in the same AZ to replace the affected instances.

claim: If new instances cannot be brought up in the AZ, OpenSearch Service brings up new instances in the other available AZs, provided the domain is configured to deploy instances across multiple AZs.
question: What happens when OpenSearch Service cannot replace instances in the affected AZ?

evidence.quote: In the rare event that new instances cannot be brought up in the AZ, Amazon OpenSearch Service brings up new instances in the other available AZs if the domain has been configured to deploy instances across multiple AZs.

claim: Once the AZ issue resolves, OpenSearch Service rebalances the instances so that they are equally distributed across the AZs configured for the domain.
question: What does OpenSearch Service do after an AZ issue is resolved?

evidence.quote: Once the AZ issue resolves, Amazon OpenSearch Service rebalances the instances such that they are equally distributed across the AZs configured for the domain.

claim: Programs with public Internet access can reach a domain through a public endpoint; if your data center is connected to Amazon VPC through Direct Connect or SSH tunneling you can also use VPC access, and in both cases IAM policies and security groups control access from servers outside AWS.
question: Can programs running on servers in your own data center access OpenSearch Service domains?

evidence.quote: The programs with public Internet access can access Amazon OpenSearch Service domains through a public endpoint. If your data center is already connected to Amazon VPC through Direct Connect or SSH tunneling, you can also use VPC access. In both cases, you can configure IAM policies and security groups to allow programs running on servers outside of AWS to access your Amazon OpenSearch Service domains.

claim: You control the scaling of an OpenSearch Service domain using the console, API, and CLI, by adding, removing, or modifying instances or storage volumes depending on your application needs.
question: How can you scale an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain?

values.display: adding, removing, or modifying instances or storage volumes

evidence.quote: Amazon OpenSearch Service allows you to control the scaling of your Amazon OpenSearch Service domains using the console, API, and CLI. You can scale your Amazon OpenSearch Service domain by adding, removing, or modifying instances or storage volumes depending on your application needs.

claim: Scaling an OpenSearch Service domain by adding or modifying instances and storage volumes is an online operation that does not require any downtime.
question: Does scaling an OpenSearch Service domain require downtime?

values.display: online operation that does not require any downtime

evidence.quote: No. Scaling your Amazon OpenSearch Service domain by adding or modifying instances, and storage volumes is an online operation that does not require any downtime.

claim: By default, OpenSearch Service automatically creates hourly snapshots of each domain and retains them for 14 days.

values.display: hourly snapshots of each Amazon OpenSearch Service domain

claim: OpenSearch Service retains the last 14 days worth of automated hourly snapshots.

values.display: last 14 days worth of automated hourly snapshots
